subject: Performance review follow-up: confidential conduct concern
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance review follow-up: confidential conduct concern

Monica / Lauren —

I wanted to flag a sensitive situation that came up in yesterday's performance conversation with Neha Kapoor. After going through the feedback, Neha disclosed an interaction she says made her uncomfortable with a peer on the team. She asked that this be kept confidential while we determine next steps — she is worried about potential retaliation and asked to pause the formal ratings conversation until HR reviews.

High level:
- Timeline: incident described as occurring two weeks ago during a late-hour Slack exchange.
- Evidence: she saved a short thread and a screenshot; asked me not to forward until intake is complete.
- Impact: says it affected her willingness to participate in the review; requested temporary reassignment of a weekly sync.

I've attached a redacted extract from the review call notes and a separate chat-log extract for intake (review-extract.pdf, chat-log.txt).

I want to be careful and follow HR protocol here. Can you advise next steps for intake and whether we should pause any performance calibration conversations or 1:1 notes being shared with the broader manager group?

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior PM, Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance review follow-up: confidential conduct concern

Thanks Marcus — and thanks for handling this sensitively.

I have opened an intake record (HR-Case-#2026-NEHA-INTAKE) and will start the standard confidentiality-first process. Immediate asks:
1) Please do not circulate the attachments outside this thread — I'll pull them into the HR intake folder myself.
2) Temporarily pause any calibration notes or public doc changes related to Neha's review until HR confirms.
3) Can you confirm whether Neha is currently reporting directly to you or to another manager for day-to-day work? (From your note it sounds like you are the review owner.)

I'll schedule an intake call with Neha today or tomorrow and will include a brief on no-retaliation protections. If intake suggests an investigatory interview, we will coordinate interview times and let managers know only on a need-to-know basis. I am cc'ing Lauren for legal input on sensitive evidence handling.

— Monica
Monica Patel

Monica —

Quick answers: I am Neha's direct manager and was running the performance conversation yesterday. She asked me to hold off on sharing the review doc and asked that we not remove her from projects at this time — only to adjust certain meeting assignments that overlap with the other person. She has not asked for formal separation; her ask was precautionary.

For intake, I've attached the extracts to this thread (review-extract.pdf, chat-log.txt) and included one screenshot (screenshot-1.png). The chat extract is timestamped and not redacted in places — please redact as needed for the intake folder.

If it helps, I'll draft a short note to Neha confirming our next steps and the confidentiality safeguards, but would prefer HR lead that communication.

On a related note: given the timing (mid-cycle reviews) I'm concerned about unintentional bias leaking into calibration. Please advise if I should pause entering any ratings or PIPs until HR confirms next steps.

Marcus

Thank you for the heads up. A few legal/PR safeguards while HR completes intake:
- Do not alter any formal performance records or calibration notes until HR confirms. If a pause is required, HR will mark the record.
- Preserve original files — Marcus, please avoid editing the attachments you shared. HR will ingest originals into a secure evidence store.
- We will issue a standard confidentiality and no-retaliation reminder to the small distribution that is strictly necessary (intake team + legal).

Monica — please confirm whether you want external counsel involved at intake. cc'ing Emma from EmploymentLaw for quick availability.

Lauren Bishop

Monica / Lauren —

Quick update from my side after the intake call earlier today with Neha: she appreciated the privacy-first approach and confirmed she wants HR to proceed with a limited investigatory interview. She also asked that we postpone any calibration discussions involving her role until HR closes the intake — I have placed a hold on the internal review doc and notified the calibration lead.

Next steps I've committed to:
- Keep the specific details of the intake restricted to HR + Legal + the intake investigator.
- Remove Neha from the weekly sync with the other party and reassign coordination to Evelyn for two weeks (Evelyn, thanks).
- Make no changes to compensation or writeups pending HR's guidance.

Monica — please advise when interview slots are available; I'm flexible next week afternoons. If you want me to draft a neutral manager note to Neha reiterating protections, tell me and I'll send.

Thanks — Marcus
